deviations.mechanism: op-revm fee distribution: the OP handler's reward_beneficiary
deviations.reason: After every non-deposit transaction op-revm credits the base fee, the L1 data fee and the operator fee to the BaseFeeVault (0x…19), L1FeeVault (0x…1a) and OperatorFeeVault (0x…1b) predeploys with balance_incr, which touches each vault even when the amount is zero. The corpus runs with zero fees, so each vault is touched and stays empty; revm 43's mainnet handler has no vaults. EIP-161 state clearing drops a touched empty account when the state is committed (tests/claims.rs checks it), so the difference never reaches the state root. An effect stops matching once a transaction pays a non-zero fee of its kind: the vault then holds a balance and the difference must be attributed again.

deviations.mechanism: op-revm's Karst precompile set: the BN254 pairing (0x08) rejects inputs over 57,600 bytes
deviations.reason: op-revm bounds the BN254 pairing input on OP chains (57,600 bytes, 300 pairs, from Karst on); a longer input fails the precompile, which consumes the gas the call forwarded. Ethereum's pairing has no such bound, so revm 43 runs the 301 pairs and returns 1. The scenario's proxy records the failure: it stores no success flag and no return size, and the hash of empty return data. The failed call also leaves the precompile account untouched.
